subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A medical student is asked to list the normal constituents of bile during a physiology review session.
question: Which of the following is a complete and correct list of the major constituents of bile?

options.text: Bile salts, bilirubin, and pancreatic lipase only
Cholesterol, phospholipids, and intrinsic factor
Gastrin, secretin, bicarbonate, and water
Bile salts, phospholipids, cholesterol, bilirubin, water, and ions
Bile acids, pepsinogen, and gastric mucus

explanation_correct: Bile is composed of bile salts, phospholipids, cholesterol, bilirubin, water, and ions. Bile salts are bile acids conjugated to glycine or taurine, which makes them water soluble. This composition allows bile to solubilize lipids and to serve as the route for excretion of bilirubin and cholesterol.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pancreatic lipase is a pancreatic enzyme, not a constituent of bile, and this list omits phospholipids and cholesterol.
explanation_incorrect.B: Intrinsic factor is secreted by gastric parietal cells, not found in bile.
explanation_incorrect.C: Gastrin and secretin are hormones, not biliary constituents; bicarbonate is prominent in pancreatic and duodenal secretions.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pepsinogen comes from gastric chief cells and gastric mucus from mucosal cells; neither is a normal bile constituent.

educationalObjective: Bile contains bile salts, phospholipids, cholesterol, bilirubin, water, and ions.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A researcher studies a patient on a high-cholesterol diet and observes an increased conversion of cholesterol into bile acids. She wants to identify the enzyme that controls the rate of this pathway.
question: Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of bile acid synthesis?

options.text: HMG-CoA reductase
Cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase
UDP-glucuronosyltransferase
Heme oxygenase
Pancreatic lipase

explanation_correct: Cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting step in bile acid synthesis, converting cholesterol into bile acids in the liver. This is the key regulatory point for the pathway that generates the bile salts needed for lipid digestion and absorption.

explanation_incorrect.A: HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis, not of bile acid synthesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: UDP-glucuronosyltransferase conjugates bilirubin with glucuronate in hepatocytes; it is not part of bile acid synthesis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Heme oxygenase converts heme to biliverdin in the pathway of bilirubin production.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pancreatic lipase digests dietary triglycerides in the intestinal lumen and does not synthesize bile acids.

educationalObjective: Cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme of bile acid synthesis.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 34-year-old woman with Crohn disease involving the terminal ileum develops frequent watery stools and passes calcium oxalate kidney stones. Her physician suspects both problems stem from the same underlying absorptive defect.
question: Which sequence best links her ileal disease to these two complications?

options.text: Reduced ileal bile salt absorption leads to bile acid diarrhea and fat malabsorption; calcium binds fat instead of oxalate, so free oxalate is absorbed and calcium oxalate stones form
Reduced ileal bile salt absorption lowers hepatic cholesterol synthesis, which increases urinary oxalate excretion
Increased ileal bile salt absorption increases fat absorption and promotes calcium oxalate stone formation
Reduced pancreatic bicarbonate secretion impairs fat digestion and increases oxalate secretion into the urine
Increased colonic bile salts increase water absorption, causing constipation and calcium-containing stones

explanation_correct: Reduced absorption of enteric bile salts at the distal ileum, as occurs in short bowel syndrome or Crohn disease, prevents normal fat absorption and may cause bile acid diarrhea. Calcium normally binds oxalate in the gut, but when fat is malabsorbed calcium binds fat instead, leaving free oxalate to be absorbed. Hyperoxaluria then increases the frequency of calcium oxalate kidney stones.

explanation_incorrect.B: The mechanism is oxalate malhandling from fat malabsorption, not a change in hepatic cholesterol synthesis driven by bile salt loss.
explanation_incorrect.C: The problem is reduced, not increased, ileal bile salt absorption; increased fat absorption would not produce this pattern.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pancreatic bicarbonate deficiency causes steatorrhea, but it does not link ileal disease to oxalate stone formation through urinary oxalate secretion.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bile acids in the colon promote secretion rather than water absorption, and constipation is not the typical outcome of ileal bile salt malabsorption.

educationalObjective: Ileal bile salt malabsorption causes bile acid diarrhea and calcium oxalate stones because calcium binds unabsorbed fat, leaving free oxalate to be absorbed.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 58-year-old man has a malignant obstruction of the common bile duct. No bile reaches the duodenum, and he develops steatorrhea and difficulty maintaining normal vitamin D status.
question: Which function of bile is most directly impaired in this patient?

options.text: Digestion of dietary starch by pancreatic amylase
Absorption of monosaccharides via SGLT1
Secretion of gastric acid by parietal cells
Conjugation of bilirubin within hepatocytes
Digestion and absorption of lipids and fat-soluble vitamins

explanation_correct: Bile is required for the digestion and absorption of lipids and fat-soluble vitamins, which explains steatorrhea and impaired vitamin D status when bile is excluded from the gut. Bile also serves as the body's primary route for bilirubin and cholesterol excretion and has antimicrobial activity through membrane disruption.

explanation_incorrect.A: Starch digestion is carried out by pancreatic alpha-amylase, which does not require bile.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glucose and galactose absorption via SGLT1 is a brush-border transport process independent of bile salts.
explanation_incorrect.C: Gastric acid secretion by parietal cells is regulated by histamine, gastrin, and acetylcholine, not by bile.
explanation_incorrect.D: Bilirubin conjugation by UDP-glucuronosyltransferase occurs inside hepatocytes and continues even when bile flow is obstructed.

educationalObjective: Bile enables lipid and fat-soluble vitamin absorption and is the main route for bilirubin and cholesterol excretion.
